mcqs.stem: Best guess: a physician invests in a restaurant partnership but never works there. Her share of the loss is $20,000, and she has no other passive income. How much can she deduct this year?

choices.explanation: That allowance applies to rental real estate.
Correct. Without material participation the loss is passive and can offset only passive income.

mcqs.explanation: Without material participation the loss is passive and can offset only passive income.

mcqs.stem: Single taxpayer, MAGI $140,000, actively participates in a rental with a $15,000 loss, no passive income. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance isn't fully phased out until $150,000.

mcqs.stem: A cabin is rented 10 days during the year and used personally the rest of the time. What is the tax treatment of the $4,000 rent?

choices.explanation: Correct. §280A(g): rented fewer than 15 days → rent excluded.

mcqs.explanation: §280A(g): rented fewer than 15 days → rent excluded.

mcqs.stem: In what order are the loss limitations applied?

choices.text: Passive, at-risk, basis, excess business loss
Excess business loss, then passive, at-risk, basis
At-risk, basis, passive, excess business loss
Basis, at-risk, passive, excess business loss

mcqs.explanation: Basis → at-risk → passive → §461(l).

mcqs.stem: A partner's basis is $40,000, including $30,000 share of nonrecourse debt (not qualified real estate financing). Her share of the loss is $25,000, and she materially participates. How much is deductible?
mcqs.explanation: Basis allows $25,000, but at-risk excludes nonrecourse debt: $10,000 allowed; $15,000 suspended under §465.

mcqs.stem: Which person qualifies as a real estate professional?

choices.text: An accountant who works 2,000 hours at her firm and 800 hours managing her rentals
choices.explanation: Real estate must be more than half of personal services.

choices.text: An investor who owns 20 rental properties managed by an agent
A full-time property manager who works 1,800 hours in real property businesses
choices.explanation: Correct. More than 750 hours and more than 50% of personal services in real property trades or businesses.

choices.text: A retiree who works 500 hours on his rentals

mcqs.explanation: More than 750 hours and more than 50% of personal services in real property trades or businesses.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer sells his entire interest in a passive activity to an unrelated buyer for a $5,000 gain. Suspended losses are $18,000. He has no other passive activities. What is the result?

choices.explanation: A full disposition frees all suspended losses.

choices.text: Losses stay suspended until other passive income
choices.explanation: A full taxable disposition releases them.

choices.text: All $18,000 of suspended losses is deductible
choices.explanation: Correct. §469(g): a fully taxable disposition to an unrelated party frees the suspended losses.

mcqs.explanation: §469(g): a fully taxable disposition to an unrelated party frees the suspended losses.

mcqs.stem: The 2025 excess business loss threshold for joint filers is $626,000. Married filing jointly, 2025 business losses of $900,000 and nonbusiness income of $1,000,000. How much business loss is disallowed under §461(l)?
mcqs.explanation: Excess business loss = 900,000 − 626,000 = 274,000, carried forward as an NOL.

mcqs.stem: A vacation home is rented 100 days and used personally 12 days. How is it classified?

choices.text: Rental property; losses subject to passive rules
choices.explanation: Correct. 12 days is not more than the greater of 14 days or 10 days (10% of 100).

mcqs.explanation: 12 days is not more than the greater of 14 days or 10 days (10% of 100).

mcqs.stem: Which amount is **not** included in a taxpayer's at-risk amount?

choices.text: Recourse debt for which the taxpayer is personally liable
choices.explanation: Personal liability makes it at risk.

choices.text: Nonrecourse loan from the seller of equipment
choices.explanation: Correct. Nonrecourse debt is generally excluded, except qualified nonrecourse real estate financing.

choices.text: Qualified nonrecourse financing on real estate from a commercial lender

mcqs.explanation: Nonrecourse debt is generally excluded, except qualified nonrecourse real estate financing.

mcqs.stem: A married couple with MAGI of $170,000 actively participates in a rental with a $10,000 loss and has $4,000 of passive income from a limited partnership. How much of the rental loss is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance is fully phased out.
Correct. Passive losses offset passive income.

mcqs.explanation: No $25,000 allowance above $150,000 MAGI; the loss offsets only the $4,000 of passive income; $6,000 is suspended.

mcqs.stem: Which activity is treated as passive regardless of participation (for a taxpayer who isn't a real estate professional)?

choices.text: A consulting business the taxpayer runs full time

choices.explanation: Correct. Rental activities are generally passive per se.

choices.text: A working interest in an oil well held directly
choices.explanation: Working interests are excluded from passive treatment.

mcqs.explanation: Rental activities are generally passive per se.

mcqs.stem: A home is rented 60 days for $9,000 and used personally 40 days. Allocated rental expenses: interest and taxes $4,000; operating $3,000; depreciation $5,000. What is the rental deduction for depreciation?

choices.explanation: Deductions are limited to rental income.

mcqs.explanation: Personal use of 40 days is more than 14 days → residence; the order is interest/taxes, operating, depreciation.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer with MAGI of $130,000 actively participates in a rental with an $18,000 loss and has no passive income. How much is deductible?
mcqs.explanation: The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of MAGI over $100,000: $25,000 − $15,000 = $10,000.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer works 520 hours a year in a business he co-owns. How are its losses treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. More than 500 hours is material participation.

choices.text: As passive unless he has 750 hours
choices.explanation: 750 hours is for real estate professionals.

mcqs.explanation: Participation of more than 500 hours in the year is material participation, so the activity isn't passive.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer rents a beach condo to guests whose average stay is 5 days. How is it treated under the passive rules?

choices.explanation: Correct. Average use of 7 days or less isn't a rental activity.

mcqs.explanation: An activity with average customer use of 7 days or less isn't a rental activity; it's passive only if the taxpayer doesn't materially participate.

mcqs.stem: A high-income taxpayer has a $20,000 passive loss and $15,000 of passive income from a limited partnership. What is the result?

choices.explanation: Correct. Passive losses offset passive income.

mcqs.explanation: Passive losses are deductible against passive income; the excess is suspended and carried forward.

mcqs.stem: For 2025, the excess business loss threshold for a single filer is $313,000. A single filer has a $500,000 business loss and large other income. What happens?

choices.explanation: Correct. The excess loss carries forward.
It carries forward as an NOL.

mcqs.explanation: §461(l): business losses over the threshold are disallowed and carried forward as an NOL.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer has $5,000 of passive activity credits but no tax on passive income. What happens?

choices.explanation: Correct. They offset only tax on passive income.

mcqs.explanation: Passive activity credits can offset only the tax attributable to passive income; unused credits carry forward.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer sells his passive rental to his brother at a loss. What happens to the suspended losses?

choices.explanation: Correct. A related-party sale doesn't free them.

mcqs.explanation: Suspended losses are freed only on a fully taxable disposition to an unrelated party.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer works 120 hours in an activity, more than anyone else. Does she materially participate?

choices.explanation: Correct. Over 100 hours and not less than anyone else.
That isn't what the rule says.

mcqs.explanation: One material participation test is more than 100 hours and not less than any other individual.

mcqs.stem: An owner rents a building to a C corporation in which he materially participates. How is the net rental income treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. The self-rental rule recharacterizes it.

mcqs.explanation: Net income from renting property to a business in which the taxpayer materially participates is nonpassive.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer dies with $40,000 of suspended passive losses. His heirs get a $25,000 basis step-up on the activity. How much loss is deductible on the final return?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses above the step-up are deductible.

mcqs.explanation: At death, suspended losses are deductible only to the extent they exceed the basis step-up.

mcqs.stem: A married taxpayer files separately and lived apart from his spouse all year. He actively participates in a rental with a $15,000 loss; his MAGI is $40,000. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. The special allowance is halved for MFS living apart.

mcqs.explanation: Married filing separately taxpayers who lived apart all year get a $12,500 allowance, phased out from $50,000 MAGI.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer owns a restaurant and a bakery in the same town with common ownership and shared management. How may they be treated under the passive rules?

choices.explanation: Correct. Activities forming an appropriate economic unit may be grouped.

mcqs.explanation: Taxpayers may group activities that form an appropriate economic unit, affecting material participation.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer sells his entire passive rental to an unrelated buyer on the installment method, recognizing 40% of the gain this year. He has $30,000 of suspended losses. How many are freed this year?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses are freed in proportion to gain recognized.

mcqs.explanation: On an installment disposition, suspended losses are allowed in the ratio of gain recognized each year to total gain.

mcqs.stem: How many hours of participation in an activity meets the main material participation test?

choices.explanation: Correct. More than 500 hours a year.

mcqs.explanation: Participating more than 500 hours in a year is material participation.

mcqs.stem: What does the real estate professional test require?

choices.text: Over 750 hours and half of work
choices.explanation: Correct. Both tests must be met.

mcqs.explanation: A real estate professional performs more than 750 hours and more than half of personal services in real property trades.

mcqs.stem: Rental income from a home rented for how few days can be excluded?
mcqs.explanation: Income from renting a residence for fewer than 15 days a year is excluded.

mcqs.stem: An active participant has MAGI of $120,000. What is the maximum rental loss allowance?
mcqs.explanation: The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of MAGI over $100,000.

mcqs.stem: An active participant with MAGI of $90,000 has a $30,000 rental loss and no passive income. What is deductible?
mcqs.explanation: Losses above the allowance are suspended until passive income or a disposition.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer sells a passive activity with $40,000 of suspended losses to an unrelated buyer. What happens to the losses?

choices.explanation: Correct. A complete taxable disposition frees them.
All of the losses are freed.

mcqs.explanation: A fully taxable disposition to an unrelated party frees all suspended losses of the activity.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer has $10,000 of passive income and an $18,000 passive loss from another activity. What is suspended?

choices.explanation: Correct. Passive losses offset passive income.

mcqs.explanation: Passive losses can offset passive income from other activities; the excess is suspended.

mcqs.stem: A vacation home is rented 90 days and used personally 30 days. Non-interest expenses are $12,000. How much is allocated to rental under the IRS method?
mcqs.explanation: Expenses are allocated by rental days over total use days.

mcqs.stem: A home is used personally 30 days and rented 90 days, so it's a residence. Rental income is $8,000, and allocated expenses are $11,000. What is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. Deductions are limited to rental income.

mcqs.explanation: When a rental home is also a residence, rental deductions can't exceed rental income.

mcqs.stem: A short-term rental has an average stay of 5 days, and the owner materially participates. How is the income or loss treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. It isn't a rental activity under §469.

mcqs.explanation: Rentals with average stays of 7 days or less aren't rental activities, so material participation can make them nonpassive.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer invests $20,000 cash plus a $50,000 nonrecourse loan (not qualified real estate financing) and has a $40,000 loss. How much is allowed under the at-risk rules?

choices.explanation: Limited to the amount at risk.
Correct. Nonrecourse debt isn't at risk.

mcqs.explanation: Losses are limited to the amount at risk, which excludes most nonrecourse debt.

mcqs.stem: A real estate investor uses qualified nonrecourse financing from a bank. Does it count as at risk?

choices.explanation: Correct. Qualified real estate financing is at risk.

mcqs.explanation: Qualified nonrecourse financing for real estate is treated as at risk.

mcqs.stem: A real estate professional who materially participates has a $60,000 rental loss. How much is deductible against wages?
mcqs.explanation: Rental losses of a real estate professional who materially participates are nonpassive.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer has a $400,000 business loss and $50,000 of other income in 2025. The threshold is $313,000. How much is an excess business loss?
mcqs.explanation: Excess business losses above the threshold are disallowed and carried forward as an NOL.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer gives a passive activity with $15,000 of suspended losses to her son. What happens to the losses?

choices.text: They add to the son's basis
choices.explanation: Correct. They can't be deducted by either.

mcqs.explanation: Suspended losses on gifted passive property are added to the donee's basis.

mcqs.stem: An owner runs several related businesses and wants to meet material participation. What may help?
mcqs.explanation: Grouping activities as an appropriate economic unit lets hours be combined.

mcqs.stem: A married couple wants rental losses treated as nonpassive. How are their hours counted?
mcqs.explanation: One spouse must meet the REP tests alone, but spouses' hours combine for material participation.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer with large suspended passive losses expects a high-income year. When should she sell the activity?

choices.explanation: Correct. Freed losses offset high-rate income.

mcqs.explanation: Freed suspended losses are most valuable in high-income years.

mcqs.stem: A passive activity is sold on the installment method. When are its suspended losses released?
mcqs.explanation: Installment dispositions free suspended losses in the ratio of gain recognized to total gain.

mcqs.stem: An owner dies with $50,000 of suspended passive losses. The property's basis steps up by $30,000. How much is deductible on the final return?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses above the step-up are deductible.

mcqs.explanation: At death, suspended losses are deductible to the extent they exceed the basis step-up.

mcqs.stem: An investor has losses from a publicly traded partnership. What may they offset?
mcqs.explanation: PTP losses can offset only income from the same PTP.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer with MAGI of $110,000 actively participates in a rental that lost $28,000. She has no passive income. How much loss is deductible?
A taxpayer has $50,000 of passive income from a limited partnership and a $70,000 loss from another passive business activity. What is the result?

choices.explanation: The $25,000 allowance is for rental real estate.
Correct. Passive losses offset passive income; the excess carries forward.

mcqs.explanation: Passive losses offset passive income; the excess carries forward.

mcqs.stem: Which taxpayer's rental losses are **not** automatically passive?

choices.text: A doctor who owns and actively manages two rentals
choices.explanation: Rentals are passive unless an exception applies.

choices.text: A retiree with a rental managed by a property agent
choices.explanation: Rentals managed by an agent are passive.

choices.text: A real estate pro who materially participates
choices.explanation: Correct. §469(c)(7): a real estate professional's rentals with material participation are not passive.

choices.text: An investor in a real estate limited partnership

mcqs.explanation: §469(c)(7): a real estate professional's rentals with material participation are not passive.

mcqs.stem: A beach condo is rented 200 days and used personally 25 days. How is it treated?

choices.text: Rental property, with no personal-use limits
choices.explanation: 25 days exceeds the greater of 14 days or 20 days.

choices.text: The rent is excluded from gross income
Residence; deductions limited to rental income
choices.explanation: Correct. Personal use of 25 days > greater of 14 or 10% × 200 = 20 → residence.

mcqs.explanation: Personal use of 25 days > greater of 14 or 10% × 200 = 20 → residence.

mcqs.stem: A partner has outside basis of $30,000, is at risk for $20,000, and her passive share of loss is $(35,000). She has no passive income. How much can she deduct?

choices.explanation: At-risk and passive limits also apply.
Correct. After basis (30,000) and at-risk (20,000), the passive limit suspends the rest because there is no passive income.

mcqs.explanation: After basis (30,000) and at-risk (20,000), the passive limit suspends the rest because there is no passive income.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer with MAGI of $130,000 actively participates in a rental with a $20,000 loss and has no passive income. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance isn't fully phased out.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer who actively participates in a rental property has a $22,000 rental loss and 2025 MAGI of $120,000, with no other passive income. How much of the loss is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance is reduced above $100,000 of MAGI.
The deduction can't exceed the loss or the reduced allowance.
Correct. The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% × (120,000 − 100,000) = 10,000.
Active participants get the special allowance.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §469(i): up to $25,000 of rental losses for active participants, phased out by 50% of MAGI over $100,000.

mcqs.stem: An investor contributes $20,000 cash to an equipment-leasing activity, borrows $30,000 for which he is personally liable, and is allocated $50,000 of nonrecourse debt (not qualified real estate financing). What is his amount at risk?

choices.explanation: Nonrecourse debt isn't at risk outside qualified real estate financing.
Correct. Cash plus recourse borrowing; nonrecourse debt isn't at risk.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §465: amounts at risk include cash and property contributed and borrowings for which the taxpayer is personally liable; nonrecourse debt (other than qualified nonrecourse real estate financing) isn't.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer qualifies as a real estate professional. Which statement about her rental real estate losses is correct?

choices.text: They are passive and limited to $25,000
choices.explanation: The professional exception removes per se passive treatment.

choices.text: They are deductible without regard to participation
They are capital losses limited to $3,000

choices.explanation: Correct. Real estate professionals who materially participate treat rentals as nonpassive.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §469(c)(7): a taxpayer with more than 750 hours and more than half of personal services in real property trades treats rentals in which she materially participates as nonpassive.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer sells her entire interest in a passive activity to an unrelated buyer in a taxable sale. What happens to $30,000 of suspended passive losses?

choices.text: They are fully deductible in the year of sale
choices.explanation: Correct. A complete taxable disposition frees all suspended losses.

choices.text: They carry over to her other passive activities
They offset only passive income in later years

mcqs.explanation: IRC §469(g): on a fully taxable disposition of the entire interest to an unrelated party, suspended losses are allowed in full.

flashcards.back: Basis → at-risk → passive → excess business loss.
Active participation; reduced 50% of MAGI over $100,000; gone at $150,000.
> 750 hours and > 50% of personal services in real property trades.
Released on a fully taxable disposition of the entire interest to an unrelated party.
Net business losses above the threshold are disallowed for the year and carried forward as an NOL; applied after the basis, at-risk and passive limits. (The exam gives the dollar amount.)
Personal use > greater of 14 days or 10% of rental days; deductions limited to rental income.
